mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen monotonically each of the last four weeks (-32.9 to -26.7), indicating a steady reopening trend; this momentum is expected to continue, pushing the next 4-week mean above the last 4-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC increased each week from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days falls below the mean over the last 28 days despite the prior four-week uptrend.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has been recovering gradually (-21.1 to -18.7); if WORKPLACES crosses above -15 within the horizon, commuting-linked shopping trips will push RETAIL_REC higher within 2 weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -15 percent change from baseline
failure_condition: WORKPLACES crosses -15 but RETAIL_REC does not increase in the subsequent 2 weeks relative to the prior 2 weeks.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined slightly each week (11.9 to 10.6), suggesting households are spending marginally less time at home; this incremental behavioral shift should translate into higher RETAIL_REC within 1 week as freed time converts to errands and leisure trips.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 11.9 to 10.6 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC in the week following a RESIDENTIAL decline does not rise relative to the prior week.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT remains deeply suppressed (-30.6 at t-0w) despite retail recovery; if TRANSIT fails to rise above -25 within 2 weeks, reduced access to retail corridors will cap RETAIL_REC growth, keeping the next 4-week mean flat or lower relative to the last 4-week mean.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stays below -25 percent change from baseline for 2 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -30.6 at t-0w, little improvement since t-3w
failure_condition: TRANSIT stays below -25 yet RETAIL_REC's next 4-week mean exceeds the last 4-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: The joint recovery of WORKPLACES and PARKS reflects both economic and leisure activity resuming simultaneously; when both series rise together week-on-week, the combined effect on discretionary mobility compounds, driving RETAIL_REC up more strongly than either alone would predict, over a 4-week horizon.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and PARKS both increase in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -23.3 to -13.4 while WORKPLACES rose from -21.1 to -18.7
failure_condition: WORKPLACES and PARKS both rise concurrently but RETAIL_REC's 4-week forward mean does not exceed its trailing 4-week mean by more than the sum of single-series effects.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has stayed near-flat and slightly positive (0.9 to 3.7), indicating essential-goods shopping is stable; combined with rising RETAIL_REC, this suggests a shift from essential-only to discretionary shopping, reinforcing continued RETAIL_REC growth over the next 2 weeks.
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM remains flat while RETAIL_REC's next 2-week mean fails to exceed its prior 2-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-June marks the seasonal onset of summer activity patterns; PARKS mobility typically rises seasonally through summer, and this seasonal lift in outdoor activity is accompanied by increased adjacent retail and recreation spending, raising RETAIL_REC over the next 4 weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:decision date is mid-June, start of summer season
failure_condition: PARKS continues to rise seasonally but RETAIL_REC's forward 4-week mean does not increase relative to the trailing 4-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: If a policy-driven reopening regime continues (evidenced by simultaneous improvement across WORKPLACES, PARKS, and RETAIL_REC), then sustained easing of restrictions will keep driving RETAIL_REC upward only as long as RESIDENTIAL mobility continues to decline; a reversal in RESIDENTIAL (indicating renewed restrictions or caution) would signal the regime has ended.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises week-on-week after a prior declining streak
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined steadily from 11.9 to 10.6 over four weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL rises for 2 consecutive weeks yet RETAIL_REC's forward 4-week mean still exceeds the trailing 4-week mean, or RESIDENTIAL keeps falling while RETAIL_REC does not rise.
